title: Layer 2 paste has no fidelity or size rule
description:
skills/coverage-verification/SKILL.md layer 2 now requires each row's test source pasted inline, and agents/coverage-critic.md declares the paste authoritative. Neither states a fidelity or size requirement, while SKILL.md step 4 elsewhere forbids large output landing in context.

Two failure modes:
- Dispatcher trims a 300-line test to fit and cuts the binding assertion. Critic is told the paste is authoritative, returns VACUOUS, branch is BLOCKED on a healthy test with no detection path.
- Test name repeats across files (the ambiguity layer 1 now guards). Dispatcher pastes the wrong file's test and HOLDS is recorded for a row whose real test is skipped.

Needs a stated rule: paste verbatim and complete, or if too large, name what was elided and how; and derive the paste from the same file:name binding layer 1 resolved, not a fresh lookup.

Found by adversarial review 2026-08-01.
close_reason: Fixed in 11ecd14. 2y8: layer 2 paste now bound to layer 1's resolved file:name, required verbatim and complete, elisions restricted to outside the test body and named inline; truncated paste is a dispatch defect. wpm: two canaries per batch for N>=4 (bead math was inverted -- single canary catches random sacrifice (N-1)/N; fixed for the 1/N residual). nmr: JVM scope reads the declared package + enclosing top-level type off the file, path rule kept as fallback. alm: hook correlates on the plan's own SC-ID citations against coverage docs + specs; exercised over 9 cases plus the jq-less fallback.

title: wave core: verifier CLI foundation
description: Wave core of jvm-go-verifier: CLI with versioned JSON ops, coverage parsing, ID registry, tags, record contract, evidence envelope; next-id and preflight working.
close_reason:
Wave core complete at b74f139 (base 9939466, 12 commits). All 7 task issues closed; whole-branch review clean after one fix wave. go test ./... green across 5 packages under -count=1 and -race; go vet and gofmt clean; all four plan section-6 CLI walkthroughs pass.

Contract decisions later waves inherit (made during execution, spec silent on each):
1. Coverage-source recorded fields are authored as a '## Verification' bullet list of key: value pairs with arrays as JSON arrays (keys: runner-kind, runner-root, runner-command, report-globs, baseline-evidence, baseline-sha256, live-profile, final-command). The cutover wave must update the authoring skill to emit this.
2. Every document path the verifier emits or compares is repo-root-relative and slash-separated. tags.Classify's thisDoc must match coverage.Owner.DocPath in that form; a mismatch silently classifies a feature's own IDs as foreign.
3. tags.Class has ClassUnknown as iota-0 (fail-closed) and serializes via MarshalJSON as active/retired/foreign/unknown, never as an integer.
4. The CLI reads a JSON request document only behind an explicit --request <path|-> flag; it never sniffs stdin.
5. next-id output is a deterministic array sorted by kind then area, '' for unprefixed IDs; the only kind is 'sc'.
6. evidence.SchemaVersion = 1, evidence.VerifierVersion = 0.6.0 (tracks plugin.json).
7. Module path is 'test-design'; imports read test-design/internal/...
8. preflight's layer4 count and highRiskCount are equal by construction today; layer4 needs a layer-1 gap input before it means what the spec says.
9. internal/coverage is at risk of becoming a dumping ground - when go-trace needs the table scanner, extract scanTables/headerSignature/findSection rather than growing it.

title: Coverage doc warning hook is a first-plan tripwire only
description:
hooks/coverage-doc-warning.sh passes when ANY docs/superpowers/coverage/*-coverage.md exists in the repo. From the repo's second feature onward it is permanently silent, including for a plan that genuinely skipped test-coverage-design.

Deliberate for now (matching a plan to its own doc means guessing a naming convention, and a warning that misfires gets muted) and documented as a limitation in docs/enforcement.md. But it means the hook cannot measure how often the stage is skipped, which is the evidence docs/enforcement.md says the denial hook decision depends on.

Options: correlate on the feature slug shared by the plan and coverage filenames; or read the plan's own SC-ID citations and require a doc defining them.

title: JVM scope rule cannot derive class from path when file name != class name
description:
skills/coverage-verification/references/runner-output.md scope table derives the fully-qualified class from the test file's path below the source root. Kotlin, Groovy, and Scala all permit a file name that differs from the class it declares -- OrdersSpec.kt declaring class OrderValidationTest derives ...OrdersSpec but scopes as ...OrderValidationTest.

Currently falls to gap (ambiguous) for hand resolution, which is safe (no silent bind) but noisy on any Spock or KMP suite.

Fix: read the declared class/object name from the file rather than inferring it from the path, for languages where the two can diverge.

title: No emitter for Rust in the runner-output contract
description:
runner-output.md lists a Rust name-extraction pattern and a Rust scope rule but no command under 'Emitting the contract'. A Rust project therefore cannot produce the status/scope/name contract layer 1 consumes.

Not shipped deliberately: cargo test's stable output is plain text written by parallel threads, and a sed pipeline over it drops any interleaved line, which surfaces as a false gap. The doc records the shape (test <module::path::name> ... ok|FAILED|ignored) and points at cargo nextest.

Fix: specify a cargo nextest invocation with a machine-readable format and verify it against a real crate, the way the vitest/go/junit emitters were verified.

title: Decide the denial hook after dogfood
description:
docs/enforcement.md defers a PreToolUse denial hook (which could run the full tag-and-runner-report check) because the false-denial rate is unmeasured. The warning hook now ships and denies nothing.

Revisit once the stage has real mileage. Note the warning hook's own limitation (see the first-plan-tripwire bead) means its silence is NOT evidence the stage is being followed -- do not use it as the input to this decision without fixing that first.
close_reason: Decided in 75eab7e: denial hook not shipped. Measured 2026-08-01 via hooks/measure-skip-rate.sh over 723 plans in 77 repos; in the post-stage window (git-add date >= 2026-07-31) 5/5 plans cite SC-IDs that a coverage doc or spec defines, so the skip rate is zero and a denial would deny nothing. One false fire found and fixed on the way (bare SC-0 matched inside a quoted shell fragment; pattern now requires two digits per the documented SC-nn format). Trip condition recorded in docs/enforcement.md: reopen at 3 genuine skips per rolling 20 post-stage plans.

title: Lazy critic can beat the single canary (N-1)/N of the time
description:
Layer 2 voids a batch when its canary verdicts HOLDS. A critic that verdicts one arbitrary row WEAK and stamps the rest HOLDS hits the canary only 1/N of the time, so the lazy strategy succeeds (N-1)/N. The sacrificed healthy row's WEAK is blocking, so the failure mode is a spurious BLOCKED on a clean branch rather than a false PASS -- but the guard is still weak.

Wording in agents/coverage-critic.md was softened so the rule is not stated in gameable form, but the math is unchanged. Inherent to one canary per batch.

Options: more than one canary per batch; or a canary whose correct verdict is known to be HOLDS as well as ones known WEAK, so no single-sacrifice strategy is safe.

comments.text: Math in the description is inverted. Voiding triggers on the canary being verdicted HOLDS; a lazy critic that stamps one arbitrary row WEAK and the rest HOLDS hands the canary a HOLDS with probability (N-1)/N, so it is CAUGHT (N-1)/N and escapes 1/N -- not the other way round. Fixed on the strength of the 1/N residual (20% at N=5), not the claimed (N-1)/N.
